seen/problem: A model with rotary positions learns from texts of up to a thousand tokens. Hand it one of four thousand, and past the first thousand, its predictions can get as bad as an untrained model's. Why?
seen/slow: Follow one slow pair, which turns a tenth of a degree per position. In all of training, its arrow only swept this shaded slice, between zero and ninety nine point nine degrees.
seen/past: At position three thousand it has turned three hundred degrees, into a part of the circle training never showed it.
seen/fail: Queries and keys arrive turned in ways the model never learned to read, and the attention scores go wildly wrong.
seen/fast: Fast pairs are fine: they went round many times in training and met every angle. It is the slow ones that are pushed somewhere new.
seen/L: Write L train for the trained length, here a thousand: every position training saw was below it.
squeeze/idea: In 2023, Shouyuan Chen and colleagues at Meta turned this around. Instead of letting positions run past the trained range, squeeze the long text into it: divide every position by the same number.
squeeze/s: That number is the stretch, s: the new length over L train. Here, four thousand over a thousand: four.
squeeze/angle: So position three thousand turns as if it sat at seven hundred fifty: seventy five degrees, an angle training made.
squeeze/last: Even the last token, at three thousand nine hundred ninety nine, turns as if at nine hundred ninety nine point seven five: still below L train.
squeeze/between: Most positions now land between two whole ones: three thousand and one turns as if at seven hundred fifty point two five. Filling in between known points is called interpolation, which names the method: position interpolation. Running past them is extrapolation.
squeeze/close: The price: neighbors now sit a quarter step apart, turning zero point zero two five degrees apart instead of a tenth. So the model gets a fine-tune: a short extra round of training, on long texts, to read the finer spacing.
squeeze/llama: That is how they stretched Llama models, trained on two thousand and forty eight tokens, to read up to thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight: an s of sixteen.
squeeze/steps: The fine-tune took at most a thousand steps.
try/p: Try one. A model trained on two thousand and forty eight positions should read eight thousand one hundred ninety two. A pair turns a tenth of a degree per position. How far does it turn at position six thousand?
try/s: First the stretch: eight thousand one hundred ninety two over two thousand and forty eight is four.
try/raw: Without it, six thousand times a tenth is six hundred degrees, far past the two hundred and four point seven training reached.
try/scaled: With it, six thousand over four is fifteen hundred, times a tenth: a hundred and fifty degrees.
